log: SPHERE COVERAGE FOR CHROMATIN -- excluded volume without an integrator
rouse_gate's GNM treats the fibre as a PHANTOM chain that passes through itself. Self-avoidance
is the largest piece of physics it discards. Brute force restores it with Langevin dynamics at
~1 GPU-day/region; spheres restore it as 'spheres do not overlap' -- a geometric projection on
an ensemble drawn free from the analytic covariance. No timestep, no force law, no trajectory.
Scored against measured K562 Hi-C streamed from a 32 GB remote file by range request.
EVERY ARM IS DISTANCE-CONTROLLED: both sides z-scored within each separation bin, so 'contacts
fall off with distance' scores zero and only topology can earn anything.

is only about chromatin if this is large enough to crowd the chain -- see the overlap fraction.

A FREE Gaussian chain gives -1.5; this chain is crosslinked by loop bonds and the fit runs
over 50-2000 kb, so -1.5 is not the expectation here and the phantom
arm's -0.961 is not an error.
THE PHYSICS BEHAVES CORRECTLY: spheres steepen the decay -0.961 -> -1.096, i.e. -0.135
TOWARD the measured -1.405. Self-avoidance compacts the chain exactly as it should.
It closes 30% of the gap to the data -- real, and not enough to matter
for contact prediction, which is the distinction the correlation table makes.
READING
SELF-AVOIDANCE CHANGES NOTHING AT THIS SCALE. spheres 0.095 vs phantom 0.100. The
phantom approximation was adequate at 25 kb, so rouse_gate was right to skip it and the
redundancy against CTCF counting was NOT caused by the missing physics. Restoring it by
brute force would have bought the same nothing at a GPU-day per region.
BUT THE TOPOLOGY ITSELF IS NOT NOTHING: +0.100 against -0.011 for the same
anchors relocated at matched count and spacing. WHERE the loops are carries the signal; the
null sits at zero, so the polymer model earns its number -- excluded volume just is not the
part that earns it.
